keyFindings.description: Fast-follow, the one worth doing first of this round's four, and the same class as the gap this round closed. slackOwnWordsOnly's visitor assigns rather than accumulates — `ownWords = strings.Contains(own, piece)` — so its answer is correct only because the producer stops at the first false. The deep review mutated the array arm's guarded recursive call to an unconditional one and the whole TestSlack* suite stayed green; a probe then failed, with own text 'Build failed' and a rich_text section whose segments are 'FAIL TestFoo at line 42' then 'Build failed' delivering 'Build failed' instead of 'Build failed\nFAIL TestFoo at line 42', because the later match overwrote the earlier non-match and the whole block was skipped. Production is correct today. The table has the repeated-words-first ordering and the new-content-alone case but not new-before-own, which is the ordering that would catch it; the predicate would also be robust written as an accumulation.

Fast-follow: the cap fixtures assert the capped output and the body_truncated flag but not the traversal's early stop. Changing full() to return false always left the whole TestSlack* suite green, because slackPayload's capBody produces the same delivered string either way; the work bound would be removable with CI green. A deterministic early-termination assertion closes it — own text already past 2,048 runes followed by an attachment tail, which the guard skips today.

Fast-follow, coverage: no fixture carries pretext or footer, though both are ranked display names; no fixture puts two competing unranked containers in one object, so the alphabetical tail order is unpinned; the cap fixtures are ASCII only, so runes against bytes is unpinned; and no fixture places a piece after one that brings the text to exactly 2,048 runes, so stopping at equality against stopping after overflow is unpinned. Each is a case to add, not a defect: an attachment {pretext, title, text, footer} expecting all four in rank; an invented block {type: future, z: {text: last}, a: {text: first}} expecting 'first\nlast'; own text of 1,000 three-byte runes plus an attachment tail expecting no truncation; own text of 2,048 runes plus a tail expecting the own runes with body_truncated.

Recorded and unchanged, carried forward rather than re-derived: the architect's ruled items stand exactly as round 5 recorded them, with the bodies and numbers unchanged — slackWalkFallback's closure per enclosing fallback-carrying object (the tester's 1.44 s at 9,900 levels in 373 KB, the reviewer's worst shapes 59 ms and 31 ms), reachable only through a shape Slack does not produce; the fallback rule keying on the name rather than on being an attachment; the ownWords drop orphaning a field label; two objects saying the same thing both delivering; the one-line own text disagreeing with its rich_text copy, which five thermonuclear passes have now failed to produce from a client; a context element carrying only a link's url; and the Security[prompt] link-unfurl chain, where the controller is not on the path and JSON string encoding is the delimiter that holds.
